## Findings
- claim-1: The full-coordinate Hopf input gives coproduct/antipode identities in \(\Lambda\), with \(S(s_\lambda)=(-1)^{|\lambda|}s_{\lambda'}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 702-735]
- claim-2: The full-coordinate row map is \(T(A_{\lambda,\theta})=\bar s_\lambda\otimes\bar s_\theta\), and decomposable rows map to \(\mathrm{CP}(\bar s_{\nu_B}\otimes\bar s_{\nu_R})\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 373-397]
- claim-3: The intended statement is: for \(q=n-r\), \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\), and \(\rho=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_a)\subseteq b^a\), \[ [\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}]=(-1)^{|\rho|} [\bar s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}]\quad\text{in }Q. \tag{E} \] Here \(\rho'_k=\#\{\ell:\rho_\ell\ge k\}\); zero parts are omitted; and \(i^0\) is omitted when \(b=j\).
- claim-4: Both partitions in (E) lie in \(q^r\): \((i^j,\rho)\) has width at most \(i\le q\) and length at most \(j+a\le r\); the right partition has width at most \(i+a\le q\) and length \(j\le r\).
- claim-5: Define the two-sided rectangle attachment \[ \operatorname{Att}_{i,j}(\sigma,\tau) :=(i+\tau'_1,\ldots,i+\tau'_b,i^{j-b},\sigma), \qquad \sigma,\tau\subseteq b^a. \] Then \(\operatorname{Att}_{i,j}(\rho,\varnothing)=(i^j,\rho)\) and \(\operatorname{Att}_{i,j}(\varnothing,\rho)=(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})\).
- claim-6: The supplied Hopf identity does not itself supply a termwise identity \[ s_{(i^j,\rho)}-(-1)^{|\rho|}s_{\operatorname{Att}_{i,j}(\varnothing,\rho)} \in\sum_{\sigma\subsetneq\rho}\Lambda_{|\rho|-|\sigma|}s_{(i^j,\sigma)}. \tag{R} \] Its terms are tensors/row vectors \(\mathrm{CP}(s_\lambda\otimes s_{\mu'})\), whereas (R) requires a separately defined and proved map from those terms to Schur-function multiples with lower attachment \(\sigma\).
- claim-7: No supplied source passage, accepted full-coordinate row identity, or graded-kernel presentation provides the required coefficients \(F_{\rho,\sigma}\), proves their integrality, or proves that all non-endpoint terms in (R) have \(\sigma\subsetneq\rho\).
## Strategy
Let \(q=n-r\), pad \(\rho\subseteq b^a\) to \(a\) parts, and set
\[
\rho'_k=\#\{\ell:\rho_\ell\ge k\}\quad(1\le k\le b).
\]
Define
\[
\operatorname{Att}_{i,j}(\sigma,\tau)
=(i+\tau'_1,\ldots,i+\tau'_b,i^{\,j-b},\sigma).
\]
Thus \(L_\rho=\operatorname{Att}_{i,j}(\rho,\varnothing)=(i^j,\rho)\) and
\(R_\rho=\operatorname{Att}_{i,j}(\varnothing,\rho)\). Zero parts, including \(i^0\) when \(b=j\), are omitted. The intended claim is
\[
[\bar s_{L_\rho}]=(-1)^{|\rho|}[\bar s_{R_\rho}]\quad\text{in }Q.
\]
Both shapes lie in \(q^r\) under \(a+j\le r,\ a+i\le q,\ b\le i,j\).

## Gaps
The required stronger containment
\[
s_{L_\rho}-(-1)^{|\rho|}s_{R_\rho}
\in\sum_{\sigma\subsetneq\rho}
\Lambda_{|\rho|-|\sigma|}s_{L_\sigma}
\]
has not been derived. The accepted Hopf/full-coordinate identity concerns tensors
\(\mathrm{CP}(s_\lambda\otimes s_{\mu'})\) and linear-system rows; no defined map sends those terms to the asserted attached Schur multiples.

Consequently, no checkable coefficients \(F_{\rho,\sigma}\), no termwise proof of endpoint coefficients \(1\) and \(-(-1)^{|\rho|}\), and no proof that all residual attachments satisfy \(\sigma\subsetneq\rho\) are available. Integrality of such hypothetical coefficients is likewise unproved. The graded-kernel presentation cannot determine the coordinates of \([\bar s_{R_\rho}]\) in the lower-adjoined basis.

The cases \(\rho=\varnothing\) (and hence \(a=0\)) would be tautological if the statement were proved; finite checks in one specialization do not settle all parameters. Therefore this certificate is **not established and not disproved** by the supplied evidence.

## Next
A valid completion requires either an explicit determinantal/Plücker expansion defining integral \(F_{\rho,\sigma}\) and proving the displayed containment termwise, or a counterexample to that containment or to the equation in \(Q\).
